docs.summary: Drives GameObject-UI input. A scene needs exactly one enabled [`EventSystem`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.EventSystem) for its [`GameCanvas`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameCanvas)es to receive pointer and keyboard events. Each frame it hit-tests the pointer against the scene's canvases (via `UIRaycaster`) and dispatches enter/exit, press, drag, click, scroll, submit/cancel and selection events to the components under it.
docs.remarks: This is entirely game-space: it ticks from [`Update`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.EventSystem~Update) (play mode only) and nothing in the engine loop drives it. A [`GameCanvas`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameCanvas) has no dependency on it - delete this component and canvases still render, they just stop receiving input - so you can drop in your own event system. Access the active one through [`Current`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.EventSystem~Current).

docs.summary: The active event system driving UI input, or null when none is enabled.
Pixels the pointer must move after a press before it counts as a drag.
Seconds within which a repeat click on the same target increments the click streak.

The active host viewport, or `null` when running standalone (no editor). Hosts (the editor game view) write this every frame so input is sourced from a render-target region instead of the OS window. A host that stops being active sets [`ReceivesInput`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.EventSystem.HostViewport~ReceivesInput) to false.
While set, this ray drives the pointer instead of the mouse, and only world space canvases are hit.
How far along [`WorldPointer`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.EventSystem~WorldPointer) the element under it is, or null when the ray hits nothing.
